content.overview: BNS s. 337 — Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc. BNS restatement of IPC 466. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 466. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 337 is the rule on “Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc”. The section provides that whoever forges a document or an electronic record, purporting to be a record or proceeding of or in a Court or an identity document issued by Government including voter identity card or Aadhaar Card, or a register of birth, marriage or burial, or a register kept by a public servant as such, or a certificate or document purporting to be made by a public servant in his official capacity, or an authority to institute or defend a suit, or to take any proceedings therein, or to confess judgment, or a power of attorney, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 337 exists so that “Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc” has a closed legal test in Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: False documents, forgery, using a forged electronic record, property marks.

The provision in detail
337. Whoever forges a document or an electronic record, purporting to be a record or proceeding of or in a Court or an identity document issued by Government including voter identity card or Aadhaar Card, or a register of birth, marriage or burial, or a register kept by a public servant as such, or a certificate or document purporting to be made by a public servant in his official capacity, or an authority to institute or defend a suit, or to take any proceedings therein, or to confess judgment, or a power of attorney, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Essential ingredients
1. Whoever forges a document or an electronic record, purporting to be a record or proceeding of or in a Court or an identity document issued by Government including voter identity card or Aadhaar Card, or a register of birth, marriage or burial, or a register kept by a public servant as such, or a certificate or document purporting to be made by a public servant in his official capacity, or an authority to institute or defend a suit, or to take any proceedings therein, or to confess judgment, or a power of attorney, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine

Explanations
Explanation.—For the purposes of this section, “register” includes any list, data or record of any entries maintained in the electronic form as defined in clause (r) of sub-section (1) of section 2 of the Information Technology Act, 2000

Step 1 — Identify the provision. The correct current-law cite is BNS s. 337 (Forgery of record of Court or of public register, etc), Chapter XVIII — Of Offences Relating to Documents and to Property Marks.
Step 2 — State the legal test in your own words, then list the ingredients:
   (1) Whoever forges a document or an electronic record, purporting to be a record or proceeding of or in a Court or an identity document issued by Government including voter identity card or Aadhaar Card, or a register of birth, marriage or burial, or a register kept by a public servant as such, or a certificate or document purporting to be made by a public servant in his official capacity, or an authority to institute or defend a suit, or to take any proceedings therein, or to confess judgment, or a power of attorney, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine
Step 3 — Read every Explanation. An explanation is part of the section. Omitting it leaves the analysis incomplete and vulnerable to rebuttal.
Step 4 — Map each fact to an ingredient. Write “this fact proves ingredient (a)” or “this fact is missing, so the section is not made out”.
Step 5 — Conclude. If every essential ingredient is proved and no exception covers the case, BNS s. 337 applies. If any essential ingredient fails, say so and stop. Do not invent a different section to save the answer.
